draft.title: Attention
card: Attention is the process of focusing on certain stimuli while other stimuli get less notice. We cannot process everything our senses detect at once.
Selective
focusing on one stimulus and filtering out others, such as following one voice in a noisy canteen.
Divided
splitting attention across two or more tasks at the same time, such as cooking while talking. Performance on each task can drop, especially when both are demanding.
Sustained
keeping focus on one task or stimulus over a long period, such as a lifeguard watching a pool for an hour.
draft.remember: Selective picks one thing, divided shares attention between tasks, sustained keeps it going over time.

a.q: Priya is at a busy train station. She tunes out the announcements and crowd noise to hear her friend on the phone. Which type of attention is this?
opts: Selective attention
Divided attention
Sustained attention
Perceptual set
a.why: Priya focuses on one stimulus, her friend's voice, and filters out the rest. That is selective attention. It is not divided attention, because she is not splitting focus across two tasks.
a.clue: She picks one sound and ignores the others.

b.q: Tom studies at his desk for two hours without losing focus on his maths. Which type of attention is this, and why?
opts: Sustained, because focus is held on one task over time
Selective, because he focuses on one task and ignores others
Divided, because he must work through many questions
Sustained, because he is splitting focus between two tasks
b.why: Focus is held on one task for a long period, which is sustained attention. Selective attention is the tempting choice, since he does focus on one thing, but the length of time is what defines this case.
b.clue: Which feature of the scenario is about how long he stays focused?

b.best: Sustained, because focus is held on one task over time

The clue points straight at 'how long he stays focused', which is the defining feature of sustained attention, so it gives the answer away.
